To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gaze is a tool that supports hand and arm movement in object manipulation, and that gaze control is a key component of predictive motor control in object manipulation.

gaze behavior is a critical part of the sensorimotor coordination of object manipulation and that gaze behavior serves to support the development and maintenance in memory of sensorimotor correlations that are essential for predictive control of hand movement.

the gaze behavior of people who reach for and grasp a bar and then move it to press a switch is organized around a small number of gaze targets, and gaze and hand movements are linked in terms of these targets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of sensorimotor coordination in reaching and grasping, and how it is supported by gaze.
the control of eye and hand in object manipulation and how the two modalities are coordinated in a common sensorimotor system.
the development of a computational theory of the control of eye movements in the context of object-directed manipulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gaze behavior in object manipulation is not random, but is directed to specific landmarks, is tightly coupled with hand and object movements, and serves to monitor the progress of the task.
gaze control is a critical component of the sensorimotor control of manipulation.
gaze control in object manipulation serves to mark the key positions in the environment to which the fingertips and the grasped object should be directed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gaze is a critical component of the sensorimotor control system in manipulation.
eye hand coordination during object manipulation is a function of sensorimotor task requirements and is not a fixed feature of the system.
the gaze behavior of the subject is a reflection of the sensorimotor requirements that are necessary for the task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gaze is not a passive consequence of hand movement, but an integral part of a sensorimotor system that supports the planning and control of object manipulation.
gaze and hand movement are tightly coupled during manipulation, but gaze is not a direct reflection of hand movement.

gaze is not only used for visual information gathering and for the guidance of hand movement, but that it also serves to specify and maintain a functional sensorimotor correlation structure that supports predictive control of object manipulation.
